lookback_source.quote: Review the resident's medical record for the 7-day look-back period.

lookback_notes: The item's own pages state a 7-day look-back period for record review, staff interview, and coding ("behaviors observed and/or thoughts expressed in the last 7 days"). Per the document's general convention, a 7-day observation period consists of the ARD plus the 6 previous calendar days (rai-manual-v1.20.1, p. 2-21).

coding_levels.label: Hallucinations
coding_levels.definition: Check E0100A if hallucinations were present in the last 7 days. A hallucination is the perception of the presence of something that is not actually there. It may be auditory or visual or involve smells, tastes or touch.

source.quote: Check E0100A, hallucinations: if hallucinations were present in the last 7 days. A hallucination is the perception of the presence of something that is not actually there. It may be auditory or visual or involve smells, tastes or touch.

coding_levels.label: Delusions
coding_levels.definition: Check E0100B if delusions were present in the last 7 days. A delusion is a fixed, false belief not shared by others that the resident holds true even in the face of evidence to the contrary.

source.quote: Check E0100B, delusions: if delusions were present in the last 7 days. A delusion is a fixed, false belief not shared by others that the resident holds true even in the face of evidence to the contrary.

coding_levels.label: None of the above
coding_levels.definition: Check E0100Z if no hallucinations or delusions were present in the last 7 days.

source.quote: Check E0100Z, none of the above: if no hallucinations or delusions were present in the last 7 days.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code based on behaviors observed and/or thoughts expressed in the last 7 days rather than the presence of a medical diagnosis; check all that apply.

source.quote: Code based on behaviors observed and/or thoughts expressed in the last 7 days rather than the presence of a medical diagnosis. Check all that apply.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Resident intent must not be taken into account when coding items in Section E; the section focuses on the resident's actions, not the intent of their behavior.

source.quote: Resident intent should not be taken into account when coding for items in this section.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If a belief cannot be objectively shown to be false, or it is not possible to determine whether it is false, do not code it as a delusion.

source.quote: If a belief cannot be objectively shown to be false, or it is not possible to determine whether it is false, do not code it as a delusion.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If a resident expresses a false belief but easily accepts a reasonable alternative explanation, do not code it as a delusion; if the resident continues to insist the belief is correct despite an explanation or direct evidence to the contrary, code as a delusion.

source.quote: If a resident expresses a false belief but easily accepts a reasonable alternative explanation, do not code it as a delusion. If the resident continues to insist that the belief is correct despite an explanation or direct evidence to the contrary, code as a delusion.

federal_coding_rules.rule: A false belief that is readily altered with a simple reminder (i.e., attributable to memory loss/forgetfulness rather than psychosis) does not meet the definition of a delusion; code E0100Z.

source.quote: The resident's initial false belief is readily altered with a simple reminder, suggesting that their mistaken belief is due to forgetfulness (i.e., memory loss) rather than psychosis. Because it is not a firmly held false belief, it does not fit the definition of a delusion.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Misinterpretation of a real external sound or stimulus that the resident accepts an alternative explanation for is not a fixed false belief and is not coded as a delusion (code E0100Z).

source.quote: They misinterpreted a real sound in the external environment. Because they are able to accept the alternative explanation for the cause of the sound, their report of a gunshot is not a fixed false belief and is therefore not a delusion.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Both E0100A and E0100B may be checked when both a hallucination and a delusion are present.

source.quote: Coding: E0100A would be checked and E0100B would be checked.

federal.criterion: Review the resident's medical record for the 7-day look-back period.

source.quote: Review the resident's medical record for the 7-day look-back period.

federal.criterion: Interview staff members and others who have had the opportunity to observe the resident in a variety of situations during the 7-day look-back period.

source.quote: Interview staff members and others who have had the opportunity to observe the resident in a variety of situations during the 7-day look-back period.

federal.criterion: Observe the resident during conversations and structured interviews in other assessment sections and listen for statements indicating hallucinations or expression of false beliefs (delusions).

source.quote: Observe the resident during conversations and the structured interviews in other assessment sections and listen for statements indicating an experience of hallucinations, or the expression of false beliefs (delusions).

federal.criterion: Clarify potentially false beliefs: attempt to verify facts when a plausible belief is alleged to be false, and determine whether a clearly false belief can be readily corrected by a simple explanation or evidence to the contrary (without challenging the resident).

source.quote: When a resident expresses a clearly false belief, determine if it can be readily corrected by a simple explanation of verifiable (real) facts (which may only require a simple reminder or reorientation) or demonstration of evidence to the contrary. Do not, however, challenge the resident.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The supplied pages for E0100 do not tie this item to any payment or case-mix classification.
